newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London stocks firm, dollar consolidates.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London stocks firm, dollar consolidates.

text.p: The London stock market traded within sight of its record high on Tuesday but other major European bourses put on a mixed performance and the dollar consolidated recent gains.
U.S. data provided no great shocks for markets concerned about interest rate prospects and gold revived after investors earlier took flight, sending it to its lowest for 18 months.

In a currency market on the watch for problems with European monetary union, the mark rose to 1,001.70 lire after French President Jacques Chirac said Italy might not be among the first countries to join a single European currency in 1999.
But it soon slipped back to around 996.50, below its previous close of 998. Italy responded angrily, suggesting that Chirac should stay out of Italian affairs.

Wall Street edged higher, breathing a sigh of relief after slightly weaker-than-expected data for the U.S. September National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index eased inflation fears. The index declined to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August. Economists has forecasted a reading of 52.5.

Another key barometer of the U.S. economy, the Conference Board's index of leading indicators, which is supposed to forecast economic trends six to nine months down the road, rose 0.2 percent in August after an identical 0.2 percent July gain.
The figures are leading up to Friday's key U.S. September jobs data.
Higher futures and bond prices prompted London shares to push nearer record levels and the key 4,000 level on the FTSE 100 index.

"Most people expected a steady start and consolidation at the start to the new quarter but we've been proved to be wrong. The futures came in strongly and have been trading abover 4,000 for much of the morning," said one senior trader.
"We won't have difficulty breaking the 4,000 mark in the cash market, maybe not today, but in the next day or two."
The stock market shrugged off news of a higher-than-expected British September purchasing managers index -- 53.4 against a forecast 51.9 -- which could suggest higher interest rates.
German shares ended a calm session a little firmer with investors holding back after last week's record-breaking performance.
"We are low on economic news, low on corporate news. This market is really still drawing breath after the push upward we had last week," said one Munich dealer.
French shares traded lower as investors took profits after strong gains of Monday topped advances last week.
The dollar hit 2-1/2 year highs against the yen on Monday, boosted by signs that Japan's economic revival was faltering and the gap between U.S. and Japanese interest rates was widening.

It showed a limited decline from its highs on Tuesday on profit-taking after key Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara denied that he had said Japan was unlikely to raise rates until the end of March 1997.

After comments by Finance Minister Wataru Kubo that he supported a strong dollar, not necessarily a stronger dollar, an official of his ministry said Kubo's comments did not mean Tokyo did not want the dollar to rise further against the yen.
"I think the Japanese authorities don't want to rock the boat. They want the dollar to stay around these levels," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank.
Gold traded around $379 an ounce by mid-afternoon, nearly $2 above its morning fix.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.33 yen and 1.5265 marks versus Monday's late European levels of 111.52 and 1.5255.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 28.2 points at 3,981.9 after an earlier high of 3,984.5. Its all-time peak was 3,994.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 8.72 at 2,124.09. The 30-share DAX index of German shares ended bourse floor trade up 3.88 at 2,655.73.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed firmer at $378.65 an ounce in the afternoon versus a morning fix of $377.05, its lowest since March 1995, and Monday's close of $378.60. Silver rose five cents to $4.92 and platinum was up $1 at $384.25.
